records.name: POST /api/parameter and GET /api/state (rebuild + tessellate a 2-sketch, 2-feature join)
records.host: i3-1125G4, debug build, loopback, Fedora 43, rustc 1.94.0
records.notes: Median 17.3 ms, max 17.9 ms over 20 alternating depth values on a project of rectangle + extrude + rectangle + extrude-join. The same project answered GET /api/state in 17.4 ms median. The recorded single-feature baseline on this host was 4.44 ms (bm-studio-parameter), so one boolean feature costs about 4x the request: every request rebuilds the whole graph and re-tessellates it. Correctness was checked in the same session (analytic union volume asserted by t-cad-feature-graph and t-cad-studio-m11). Harness: target/studio-qa/measure.sh.

records.name: GET /api/state, unchanged two-feature history, per-feature cache
records.host: i3-1125G4, debug build, loopback, Fedora 43, rustc 1.95.0
records.notes: Same project and client conventions as bm-studio-m11-rebuild, whose 17.4 ms this replaces: since the studio keeps a BuildCache, a repeat request reuses every prefix and only clones the mesh. 0.6–0.9 ms median and 1.1 ms max over three runs of target/studio-qa/measure-cache.sh. An edit of a parameter both features read is 18.5 ms median, i.e. a full rebuild as before (+2% measured in-process).

records.notes: 1 new-body extrude + 5 joins, last feature's depth on `diameter`: cold 30.32 ms (6 extrudes, 5 unions), cached 7.88 ms (1 extrude, 1 union), unchanged history 0.01 ms. Volumes 1500.080 and 1720.080 mm³ unchanged. Harness: cargo run --release -p cad-studio --example rebuild_bench, three warm-up rebuilds discarded, a unique parameter value before every sample.
